raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Decode workers can reuse cached prefixes, but bucket-first routing currently rejects `cache_aware` on decode groups. A repeated request can therefore go to a cold decode worker even when an eligible worker already holds the prefix.

This implements the decode-selection part of the decode-aware pairing item in #43699, related to #43098 and #25760.

## Modifications

- Allow decode groups to opt into `cache_aware` with `prefer` or `balanced` affinity. The default remains power-of-two.
- Rank admitted workers by their longest confirmed GPU-or-host prefix, then GPU-resident depth and decode load. Disk/external copies and pending placements do not count.
- Keep bucket and version-group boundaries, admission limits, and load-based fallback. Balanced mode uses running-request load.
- Limit cache affinity to single-DP-rank workers using the local radix tree. Multi-rank workers can still be selected by the load fallback; remote-index affinity needs a tier-aware API first.

The README includes the bucket configuration. Prefill selection and engine transfer behavior are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Added policy regressions for tier changes, eviction, admission, stale load, partial-page thresholds, cache-salt/LoRA isolation, and missing cache signals. An HTTP PD test checks selection within the prefill's version group and preserves the shared bootstrap room.

Passed locally on macOS arm64:

```sh
cargo +1.92.0 test --locked --release --workspace -- --skip parity_matrix
cargo +1.92.0 clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check
# From the repository root:
pre-commit run --all-files
```

The tokenizer parity tests require external fixtures and were excluded. No model accuracy or GPU serving run was performed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Added a paired CPU lookup benchmark on the same tree, with half the owners on GPU and half on host memory. Apple M4 Pro, Rust 1.92.0 release build, 20 samples, 1s warmup, 2s measurement:

| Shared prefix | Existing any-tier lookup | New resident lookup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 8 workers, 64 blocks | 8.11 us | 13.83 us |
| 32 workers, 512 blocks | 232.26 us | 360.90 us |

```sh
cargo +1.92.0 bench --locked --bench tree_lookup -- resident_prefix --sample-size 20 --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 2
```

These measure tree lookup cost, excluding token hashing and dispatch. The additional walk distinguishes GPU residency from host-backed prefixes. Reduced KV transfer and TTFT still need a real PD serving benchmark; this PR makes no claim about those gains.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add regression tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [ ] Provide GPU accuracy and serving performance results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@hzh0425 @sherlockwu, could you review the tier-selection behavior and single-rank scope for the decode-aware pairing work?

files.patch:
@@ -693,6 +693,51 @@ The legacy `--cache-threshold`, `--balance-abs-threshold`, and
 one-to-one replacements; remove them and review the current `sgl-router
 --help` output when tuning Cache-Aware routing.
 
+## Decode cache affinity (bucket-first routing)
+
+With `--chat-routing reorg --policy cache_aware --bucket-config buckets.json`,
+a decode group can opt into confirmed local-memory prefix reuse:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buckets": [{
+    "id": "pd",
+    "prefill": {"policy": "cache_aware"},
+    "decode": {
+      "policy": "cache_aware",
+      "affinity": {"mode": "balanced", "balanced_by": "running_requests"},
+      "admission": {"max_kv_usage": 0.9}
+    }
+  }]
+}
+```
+
+Prefill keeps its existing prefix policy. Decode selects the admitted worker
+with the longest confirmed GPU-or-host prefix, breaking equal-prefix ties by
+GPU-resident depth, decode load, then worker ID. The existing minimum matched
+token/ratio settings apply. Bucket membership, health, retry exclusions and
+prefill/decode version-group boundaries still constrain the candidates.
+
+Decode requires the local `radix_tree` provider and KV events from decode
+workers with decode prefix caching enabled. Disk/external-only copies and
+pending placements do not count as local-memory hits. Cache affinity currently
+applies only to workers reporting one DP rank; multi-rank workers remain eligible
+for the load-based fallback until dispatch can target the cached rank.
+
+Set the decode group's affinity mode to `prefer` or `balanced`. A missing or
+insufficient cache signal falls back to power-of-two. `prefer`
+keeps an admitted cache owner; `balanced` may choose another worker when both
+running-request load thresholds are exceeded. Decode defaults to balancing
+running requests, using that metric's default gap unless explicitly set on the
+group or inherited from a global running-request configuration. It does not
+compare prefill-token pressure. Selection reasons are `decode_cache_candidate`,
+`decode_affinity_load`, and `no_decode_cache_candidate`.
+
+The default decode policy remains power-of-two. Cache events are routing hints;
+engines still determine actual reuse. CPU policy and HTTP tests cover selection
+and fallback, but this mode needs serving benchmarks before claiming lower
+KV-transfer volume or latency.
+
